title: Counting Stable Equivalent Models in Cyclic Linear Non-Gaussian Systems
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field and NOT salvageable in scope; the four panel findings are repairable as hygiene, but repairing them does not change the 7.2 novelty ceiling.
gap_reasons: The sharp bounded-degree phase diagram is proved only for fixed-labelled matrices manufactured by the reduction, not for a natural bounded-degree class of cyclic LiNG mechanisms, so it does not establish a general sparsity frontier.

The consumer claim is correspondingly limited: the results show worst-case difficulty of stability-conditioned matching counts, but do not analyze the distribution of instances produced by the cited intervention method or provide a usable approximation scheme for its stable frequencies.

The FOBI confidence image supplies pointwise coverage but is not accompanied by a finite computational procedure for evaluating the image over its continuum of matrices and may be highly noninformative near stability boundaries, which limits its practical evidentiary value and the projected journal score.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery completed a coherent mathematical derivation of the rational 3n reduction, spectral homotopy certificate, exact and approximate counting separations, SCC factorization, exact rational enumeration, and pointwise FOBI inference. The result missed the field floor because its sharp positive frontier is confined to fixed-labelled gadget images, its consumer relevance is worst-case, and its confidence-image inversion lacks a computationally useful evaluation theorem. Formalization was not attempted because the operator's D→F freeze was active; a future re-raise needs a new natural-class, consumer-linked average-case, or computational-inference kernel rather than panel-only cleanup.
tldr: A fully observed cyclic LiNG law identifies a finite monomial row-assignment orbit, while equilibrium stability imposes a global spectral filter on that orbit. The explicit rational \(3n\)-variable construction \(W_G\) has complete stable orbit \(\{\pi_S:S\in\mathcal I(G)\}\), with graph-uniform radial margins established by a pole-free, multiplicity-preserving analytic determinant homotopy. On fixed-labelled gadget images, exact counting is in \(\mathrm{FP}\) through degree two and \(\#\mathrm P\)-complete already at degree three; approximation has a deterministic FPTAS through degree five and no FPRAS at degree six unless \(\mathrm{RP}=\mathrm{NP}\). Hardness also persists on coned gadget images whose coefficient-support digraph is one SCC, without a bounded-degree promise, so it is not caused by multiplying SCC-local counts. In contrast, the unfiltered orbit is a permanent with an FPRAS. Admissible and stable orbit counts factor exactly over SCCs for every real equation matrix; only the enumerator and its Lyapunov and bit-complexity guarantees are restricted to rational stable-reference inputs. Symmetrized FOBI-region inversion gives pointwise signed-orbit-honest count coverage, without a uniform graph-support or stability-boundary claim.
gap: Published cyclic-LiNG methods enumerate or sample the full normalized row-assignment fiber and use stability only as a candidate-level screen. They do not classify the complexity of the filtered count or justify transferring permanent-based sampling guarantees after the spectral restriction.
fill: The proposed rational graph gadget identifies stable assignments with independent sets, transfers exact and approximate counting lower bounds, factors the count over SCCs, and attaches pointwise uncertainty quantification that respects the full ICA orbit.
